---
title: "How do I shade and label a probability under a normal curve?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I shade and label a probability under a normal curve?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Specify the normal mean, standard deviation, and cutoff.

2. Calculate the tail area using pnorm().

3. Plot dnorm() and shade the matching region.

## Runnable example

```{r}
mu <- 100; sigma <- 15; cutoff <- 85
p <- pnorm(cutoff,mean=mu,sd=sigma)
curve(dnorm(x,mu,sigma),from=40,to=160,lwd=2,col="#3F78A8",
      xlab="Value",ylab="Density",main="Normal probability to the left")
xs <- seq(40,cutoff,length.out=150)
polygon(c(40,xs,cutoff),c(0,dnorm(xs,mu,sigma),0),
        col="#CEE2F0",border=NA)
abline(v=cutoff,col="#A35E20",lty=2,lwd=2)
legend("topright",legend=paste0("P(X <= 85) = ",round(p,3)),
       fill="#CEE2F0",bty="n")
print(p)
```

## Interpret the result

The shaded left-tail area equals pnorm(85,100,15), approximately 0.159. It is a probability for a normal model, not a guarantee about observations.

## Check before applying to real data

Normal modeling requires a defensible distributional assumption. The shaded area changes with mean, sd, and cutoff.
